chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, from Abu Abdillah, from his fathers, that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:
Regarding a man who converted to Islam in the middle of the month of Ramadan, he is only obligated for what he faces (i.e., the remainder of the days).

key_terms.نِصْفِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: middle of the month of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What are the fasting obligations for someone who converts to Islam during Ramadan?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (a) clarifies that a convert in the middle of Ramadan is exempt from making up the preceding days, as the obligation to fast begins from the moment of their entry into Islam. This ruling highlights the principle of gradual obligation (tadarruj) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the duty to fast and the duty to make up missed days. It underscores that the specific reward of Ramadan fasting applies only to the period after conversion, while the general obligation of fasting remains for the rest of the month.
